channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: European Government Websites Disabled Due to Vulnerability in Popular PHP Programming Language
item.description: Government websites across Europe and other nations have been taken offline following the discovery of critical vulnerabilities in the PHP programming language. Developers have released urgent patches, warning that these flaws, present for years, affect a significant portion of the internet and necessitate immediate updates or site deactivation.

item.title: New Projects and Industrial Growth Transform Kashkadarya into a Leading Region
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev visited Kashkadarya region, inspecting a new textile factory in the 'Kashkadarya' free economic zone. The $54 million project created 840 jobs and boasts advanced water and energy-saving technologies, including a closed-loop water system and solar panels, significantly reducing production costs and environmental impact.

item.title: Kazakhstan Prepares for Return of 13 Citizens from Ukraine War Zone
item.description: Thirteen Kazakh citizens, whose families advocated for their return from the conflict zone in Ukraine, are being prepared for repatriation. Lawyer Meirman Shekeev confirmed that no obstacles currently prevent their return and emphasized the need for a safe journey home. Families expressed gratitude to the President of Kazakhstan and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs for their assistance.

item.title: C5+1 Summit in Samarkand Yields Joint Statement on Partnership and Future Cooperation
item.description: The C5+1 summit in Samarkand, involving foreign ministers from the US and five Central Asian nations, concluded with a Joint Statement titled 'C5+1: Historic Partnership, Prosperous Future.' Key outcomes include enhanced trade, investment, transport cooperation via the Trans-Caspian route, collaboration on critical minerals, energy security, technology, counter-terrorism, and educational exchanges.

item.title: Turkey and Uzbekistan Adapt Cities to Changing Climate Conditions
item.description: Turkey and Uzbekistan are implementing strategies to make their cities more resilient to climate change impacts like heat, floods, and droughts. Turkey focuses on infrastructure and renewable energy, while Uzbekistan is developing New Tashkent and adapting its existing capital.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Judicial Oversight: What Judges Must Verify Before Detaining Suspects
item.description: Starting July 1, 2027, Uzbekistani judges must verify sufficient grounds for suspicion or accusation before approving detention. This reform expands judicial oversight, requiring judges to examine evidence and ensure procedural compliance, moving beyond mere legality checks.

item.title: Uzbekistan Explores Economic Diplomacy with Oman, Japan, Italy, and Germany
item.description: Uzbekistan's Ministry of Foreign Affairs is analyzing efforts to strengthen economic diplomacy. The Ambassador to Oman met with the head of the Real Estate Association to discuss cooperation. In Japan, agreements were reached to expand trade and investment. Uzbekistan showcased its tourism potential at an exhibition in Italy and discussed agricultural modernization with Germany.

item.title: Zelensky Willing to Freeze Ukraine Conflict Along Current Front Lines
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky stated his readiness to halt hostilities with Russia along the current front lines, expressing this in an interview with Fox News. He affirmed willingness to accept a peace deal that freezes the conflict, provided Ukraine retains control over at least 75% of its territory. Zelensky rejected proposals to cede Donbas for peace, emphasizing the need for diplomatic solutions based on current positions.

item.title: Tashkent Hosts Discussion on Modern Water Resource Management Technologies
item.description: Tashkent hosted an event focusing on energy efficiency, rational water resource use, and industrial technology modernization. A key aspect was the partnership between "EBA Engineering," "ARC Water & Energy," and Danish pump manufacturer "Grundfos." EBA Engineering became Grundfos's industrial sector distributor in Uzbekistan, aiming to optimize, decarbonize, and transform water management through advanced equipment and technical support.

item.title: Xinjiang Method Boosts Cotton Yields in Uzbekistan
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev visited a cotton field in Guzar district employing the Xinjiang method. This technique involves sowing cotton seeds under plastic film in double rows and using drip irrigation, reducing water use by 30-40% and fertilizer by nearly 30%. The method accelerates crop maturation by 10-15 days and increases yield significantly, with potential for 60-70 centners per hectare compared to traditional methods.

item.title: Kazakhstan and EU Trade Turnover Reaches $31.6 Billion
item.description: The 9th meeting of the Cooperation Committee on Trade between Kazakhstan and the European Union was held in Brussels. The parties discussed the current state and development prospects of trade-economic and investment cooperation. Issues of removing barriers and restrictions in mutual trade were also addressed. The implementation of the Enhanced Partnership and Cooperation Agreement was a key focus.

item.title: EU Allocates €12 Million for Essential Services in Afghanistan
item.description: The European Union has allocated €12 million to provide healthcare, nutrition, and water services to over 347,000 people in southern and southwestern Afghanistan. The assistance, delivered through INTERSOS in cooperation with other organizations, will run from June 2026 to May 2027. It aims to support vulnerable populations and prevent diseases and deaths.

item.title: EU Allocates €12 Million for Aid to Vulnerable People in Afghanistan
item.description: The European Union has allocated €12 million for vital services in health, nutrition, protection, and water and sanitation for crisis-affected people in six southern and southwestern provinces of Afghanistan. The funding will support a 12-month project benefiting 347,000 individuals, with indirect benefits for nearly 1.27 million others.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Compulsory Military Service to Be Divided into Two Stages
item.description: Kazakhstan's Armed Forces are transitioning to a two-stage model for compulsory military service. The first six months will involve basic military training in specialized centers, followed by six months of practical combat training and task execution in military units. Reforms also focus on soldier safety and rights.

item.title: Uzbekistan's New Latin Alphabet Law to Take Effect in April 2027
item.description: A new Uzbek alphabet based on Latin script, signed by the President on October 21, will come into force on April 22, 2027. Documents issued before this date will remain valid. The government has two months to develop an implementation plan for the new alphabet, which features 28 letters and an apostrophe.

item.title: Kazakhstan Approves Large-Scale Army Reform
item.description: Kazakhstan has approved a significant reform of its armed forces. The details of the reform were not immediately disclosed, but it is expected to modernize the military and enhance its capabilities. This move signals a commitment to strengthening national defense and security within the region.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Passport Ranking Declines in Henley & Partners Index
item.description: Kyrgyzstan has dropped to 81st place in the Henley & Partners Passport Index for October 2026, sharing the position with Sao Tome and Principe. Holders can access 59 destinations visa-free. This marks a decline from the 75th position earlier in the year. Kazakhstan's passport remains the strongest in Central Asia at 66th place.

item.title: President's Book on Turkmen Neutrality Published in Azerbaijani
item.description: A presentation ceremony was held for the Azerbaijani translation of President Serdar Berdimuhamedow's book 'Turkmenistan's Neutrality - A Clear Path to Peace and Trust'. The publication highlights Turkmenistan's foreign policy focused on global peace and good neighborliness, as recognized by the UN. The book details the goals and achievements of Turkmenistan's neutrality policy.

item.title: Tokayev approves military reform plan in Kazakhstan
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has approved a military reform plan for Kazakhstan. The government and Security Council are tasked with its implementation. The reform aims to create a modern, mobile, and technologically equipped army, focusing on improved command, training, personnel policy, and resource utilization. The plan incorporates international experience and domestic expertise.

item.title: New petrochemical production facilities to be launched in Kazakhstan
item.description: Kazakhstan's petrochemical industry is expanding, with production volume reaching 619,000 tons in 2025, a 73% increase from 2023. New facilities for polyethylene, urea, butadiene, and alkylate are under construction. A significant project is an integrated gas chemical complex in Atyrau region to produce 1.25 million tons of polyethylene annually.

item.title: International Oil and Gas Forum Held in Ashgabat
item.description: The "Turkmenistan Oil and Gas - 2026" international conference and exhibition has commenced in Ashgabat. Turkmenistan, a leading energy state with vast natural gas reserves, aims to expand energy partnerships and integrate innovative technologies. Organized by state concerns, the event facilitates direct relations, new projects, and global experience exchange.

item.title: Kazakhstan Approves Military Reform Plan, Dividing Conscript Service into Two Stages
item.description: Kazakhstan's President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has approved a military reform plan that includes dividing mandatory military service into two stages. The reform aims to create a modern, mobile, and technologically advanced army, addressing command, training, personnel policy, and equipment. It also introduces a dedicated ombudsman for servicemen and measures against hazing.

item.title: Kazakhstan Plans to Divide Conscript Service into Two Stages as Part of Military Reform
item.description: Kazakhstan's military reform plan includes dividing conscript service into two stages: six months of training in educational centers followed by six months of service in military units with a focus on combat readiness. The reform also involves creating Unmanned Forces, restructuring the army, and enhancing servicemen's rights, including a new ombudsman position.

item.title: Kazakhstan Adopts Military Reform Plan, Dividing Conscript Service into Two Stages
item.description: Kazakhstan has approved a military reform plan, including the creation of Unmanned Forces and a two-stage conscript service model: six months of training in educational centers and six months in military units focusing on combat readiness. President Tokayev emphasized the need for a modern, mobile, and technologically advanced army, stressing comprehensive reforms.

item.title: Afghan Representative Warns Taliban Restrictions Threaten Cultural Identity and Diversity
item.description: Afghanistan's acting UN representative, Naseer Ahmad Faiq, stated that Taliban restrictions on culture, language, music, and education endanger the nation's cultural diversity and shared identity. He noted bans on customs, artistic activities, and celebrations like Nowruz, alongside music prohibition and confiscation of instruments. Faiq also expressed concern over linguistic diversity suppression and the promotion of extremism.

item.title: Kazakhstan President Chairs Security Council Meeting on Military Reform
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev led a Security Council meeting focused on a draft military reform plan. The reform aims to modernize the armed forces, improve command, training, and technological capabilities, and enhance the army's interaction with society. The plan incorporates international experience and domestic proposals to boost the efficiency of the state's military system.

item.title: Kazakhstan Security Council Discusses Military Reform for Enhanced Discipline and Public Trust
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev chaired a Security Council meeting on military reform, focusing on a draft plan to modernize the armed forces. Key objectives include improving command, training, and technological capabilities, alongside strengthening army discipline and public trust. The reform aims for institutional changes to increase the efficiency of Kazakhstan's military organization.

item.title: Two Men Detained in Shymkent for Extorting Businessman with Threats of Arson
item.description: Two men have been arrested in Shymkent for allegedly demanding 10 million tenge from an entrepreneur. They threatened to burn him and his truck if he refused. Police apprehended the suspects while receiving half the demanded sum. A criminal case for hooliganism has been initiated, and investigations are ongoing.

item.title: Uzbek President Mirziyoyev Visits Qamashi District, Inspects Infrastructure Improvements
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev visited a neighborhood in Qamashi district, interacting with children and reviewing infrastructure development. The Chim mahalla has seen 55 billion UZS invested in improvements, including a 240-capacity kindergarten, a 640-capacity school, community and youth centers, and a park.

item.title: Uzbekistan Approves New Latin-Based Alphabet Version
item.description: Uzbekistan has officially approved a new version of its Latin-based alphabet, signed into law by President Shavkat Mirziyoyev. The updated alphabet features 28 letters and an apostrophe, reintroducing letters like Ş, Ç, Ö, and Ğ, which were previously replaced by digraphs. This reform aims to finalize the alphabet transition initiated in 1993.

item.title: Global Network Established to Support Children with Severe Illnesses, Led by Ziroat Mirziyoyeva
item.description: A Global Network for supporting children with severe and life-threatening illnesses, including cancer, was established in Samarkand. The network unites first ladies and spouses of heads of state for international cooperation and experience sharing. Ziroat Mirziyoyeva, Uzbekistan's First Lady, was elected chair for a two-year term. The initiative aims to improve childhood cancer care globally.

item.title: Chemical Accident in Ohio, USA, Forces Evacuation of Nearly a Thousand Residents
item.description: A chemical accident in Toledo, Ohio, USA, released the toxic chemical glycidyl methacrylate, used in plastics and paint production. Residents reported eye and throat irritation due to smoke and dense fog hindering emergency services. Rescuers fear a repeat explosion, while specialists are assessing air contamination levels. The cause of the explosion remains unknown.

item.title: IFC Plans to Explore Projects Worth $3 Billion in Kazakhstan by 2031
item.description: The International Finance Corporation (IFC) intends to explore projects totaling approximately $3 billion in Kazakhstan between 2026 and 2031. Around 60% of the funding is expected from private investors, with the remaining 40% from IFC's own resources. Discussions focused on transport infrastructure and the water sector, emphasizing public-private partnerships.

item.title: Safety Hazard: Bishkek Construction Company Given 3 Days to Fix Issues
item.description: A construction site in Bishkek has been found to pose a safety risk due to the removal of protective fencing around a pit. The city's architectural and construction control department issued a notice to the company, demanding the fence be restored, lighting provided, and protective structures installed within three days.

item.title: French President Macron Visits Saudi Arabia to Express Solidarity Amid Houthi Attacks
item.description: French President Emmanuel Macron made an unexpected visit to Saudi Arabia, meeting with Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman. The visit signifies France's solidarity with the Kingdom against Houthi attacks. Macron is the first Western leader to visit Saudi Arabia since the escalation of Houthi assaults. The leaders discussed energy and infrastructure cooperation.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Launches Second Phase of 'Open Cabinet' Project to Enhance Government Transparency
item.description: Kyrgyzstan has initiated the second phase of the 'Open Cabinet: Territory of Responsibility' project, aimed at increasing the openness and transparency of state bodies. The initiative seeks to strengthen public interaction and improve citizens' access to information about government operations. This phase involves open dialogues between media representatives and heads of state structures.

item.title: UNHCR Provides Carpet-Weaving Training to 70 Women in Afghanistan's Bamyan Province
item.description: The UNHCR has launched a carpet-weaving training program for 70 women in Bamyan Province, Afghanistan, with support from Italy's Ministry of Foreign Affairs. The initiative aims to equip women, including those returning from neighboring countries, with skills to earn income and support their families amidst widespread restrictions on women's rights and employment opportunities.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Offer Subsidies Up to 129,000 Tenge for Relocating Citizens Starting 2027
item.description: Starting January 1, 2027, Kazakhstan will implement new voluntary relocation rules offering subsidies up to 129,000 tenge per person. These incentives aim to improve labor force efficiency by supporting citizens, including job seekers and ethnic Kazakhs, in relocating within or between regions. Payments will cover moving costs, rent, and utilities for up to 12 months.

item.title: Kazakh Companies Dominate Central Asia's Most Valuable Companies Ranking
item.description: KazMunayGas, Kaspi.kz, and Kazatomprom lead the ranking of Central Asia's 20 most valuable companies for October 2026. Kazakh companies occupy the top seven positions, with KazMunayGas valued at $48.44 billion. Uzbekistan is represented by seven companies, led by Uzum at $2.3 billion.

item.title: Iran Intensifies Trade Relations with Central Asian Nations
item.description: Iran is actively seeking to expand trade connections with Central Asian countries. High-level officials have engaged with counterparts from four nations recently. Discussions included increasing bilateral trade volume, developing joint production ventures, and promoting the north-south trade route via the Chabahar port and railway.
